{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgzNjIwMjI5","is_bot":false,"login":"mich-murphy","name":"Michael Murphy"},"body":"## Observed

After deploying `torrent_client_reseed` (mich-murphy/home-infra#1833), every reseed call fails with:

```
upstream authentication failed
```

Tested with two valid base64 .torrent payloads (both well under the 1.4 MB schema cap), `save_path` omitted (single allow-listed path expected).

## Expected

Reseed authenticates to qBittorrent the same way the read tools do and proceeds to add-paused → recheck.

## Evidence it's write-path-specific

Same broker process, same seconds:

- `torrent_client_stats` → 200, full payload (`connection_status: connected`)
- `torrent_client_inventory` → 200, 727 items
- `torrent_client_check_paths` → 200
- `torrent_client_reseed` → `upstream authentication failed`

So the broker's stored qBittorrent credentials work for reads but not for the reseed path. Likely candidates:

- reseed path uses a different credential env var (e.g. a separate write-gated qBit password) that isn't set in the deployed environment
- write path re-authenticates instead of reusing the read path's session and hits a different (missing/wrong) secret
- write gate flag partially wired (tool registered, auth source not)

## Environment

- Broker: `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main` (deployed ~2026-09-22, 20 tools listed including `torrent_client_reseed`)
- qBittorrent: `lscr.io/linuxserver/qbittorrent:5.1.4-r3-ls453`, WebUI :8080 on internal `proxy` network
- Caller: Hermes agent on ai-dev, read tools verified working end-to-end

Filed by the Hermes agent at operator request.

358	/// At startup, when a variant carries no known `access` level.
359	fn tools(settings: &Settings) -> Vec<Tool> {
360	    let generator =
361	        SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().with(|settings| settings.inline_subschemas = true);
362	    let schema = generator.into_generator().into_root_schema_for::<ToolCall>().to_value();
363	    let variants = schema["oneOf"].as_array().expect("one schema per tool");
364	    let configured = |service: Service| settings.upstream(service).is_some();
365	    let arr =
366	        configured(Service::Sonarr) || configured(Service::Radarr) || configured(Service::Lidarr);
367	    let tool = |variant: &Value| {
368	        let (name, input) = variant["properties"].as_object()?.iter().next()?;
369	        // (enabled, read-only, destructive, idempotent)
370	        let (enabled, read_only, destructive, idempotent) = match variant["access"].as_str() {
371	            Some("arr") => (arr, true, false, true),
372	            Some("sonarr") => (configured(Service::Sonarr), true, false, true),
373	            Some("lidarr") => (configured(Service::Lidarr), true, false, true),
374	            Some("jellyfin") => (configured(Service::Jellyfin), true, false, true),
375	            Some("tautulli") => (configured(Service::Tautulli), true, false, true),
376	            Some("qbittorrent") => (configured(Service::Qbittorrent), true, false, true),
377	            Some("write") => (arr && settings.enable_requests, false, false, false),
378	            Some("toggle") => (arr && settings.enable_requests, false, false, true),
379	            Some("delete") => (arr && settings.enable_deletes, false, true, false),
380	            Some("reseed") => {
381	                (configured(Service::Qbittorrent) && settings.enable_reseeds, false, false, true)
382	            }
383	            access => panic!("tool {name} has no known access level: {access:?}"),
384	        };
385	        let hints = [read_only, destructive, idempotent, false].map(Some);
386	        let annotations = ToolAnnotations::from_raw(None, hints[0], hints[1], hints[2], hints[3]);
387	        let description = variant["description"].as_str()?.to_owned();
388	        let tool = Tool::new(name.clone(), description, Arc::new(input.as_object()?.clone()));
389	        Some(enabled.then(|| tool.with_annotations(annotations)))
390	    };
391	    let tools = variants.iter().map(|variant| tool(variant).expect("a well-formed tool schema"));
392	    tools.flatten().collect()
393	}

395	#[derive(Clone)]
396	struct Broker {
397	    client: Arc<MediaClient>,
398	    tools: Arc<Vec<Tool>>,
399	}
400	
401	impl ServerHandler for Broker {
402	    fn get_info(&self) -> ServerConfig {
403	        ServerConfig::new(ServerCapabilities::builder().enable_tools().build())
404	            .with_server_info(Implementation::new("media-broker", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
405	            .with_instructions(
406	                "Projected media inventory and playback history; media requests, \
407	                 library cleanup, and verified torrent reseeds are available only where \
408	                 explicitly enabled.",
409	            )
410	    }
411	
412	    fn list_tools(
413	        &self,
414	        _: Option<PaginatedRequestParams>,
415	        _: RequestContext<RoleServer>,
416	    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<ListToolsResult, ErrorData>> + MaybeSendFuture + '_ {
417	        std::future::ready(Ok(ListToolsResult::with_all_items(self.tools.to_vec())))
418	    }
419	
420	    /// Argument and upstream failures are sanitized `isError` results.
421	    async fn call_tool(
422	        &self,
423	        request: CallToolRequestParams,
424	        _: RequestContext<RoleServer>,
425	    ) -> Result<CallToolResponse, ErrorData> {
426	        let name = request.name.as_ref();
427	        let outcome = if self.tools.iter().any(|tool| tool.name == name) {
428	            let arguments = Value::Object(request.arguments.unwrap_or_default());
429	            match serde_path_to_error::deserialize::<_, ToolCall>(json!({name: arguments})) {
430	                Ok(call) => call.run(&self.client).await.map_err(|error| error.to_string()),
431	                Err(error) => {
432	                    let path = error.path().to_string();
433	                    let field = path.strip_prefix(name).unwrap_or(&path).trim_start_matches('.');
434	                    Err(format!("{field}: {}", error.inner()).trim_start_matches(": ").to_owned())
435	                }
436	            }
437	        } else {
438	            Err(format!("Unknown tool: {name}"))
439	        };
440	        let result = match outcome {
441	            Ok(content) => CallToolResult::structured(content),
442	            Err(message) => CallToolResult::error(vec![ContentBlock::text(message)]),
443	        };
444	        Ok(result.into())
445	    }
446	}
447	
448	/// Answer unauthenticated liveness probes with a static, data-free body.
449	///
450	/// Container health checks carry no credentials, so this one exact route runs
451	/// ahead of the bearer boundary. It returns nothing but liveness and never
452	/// touches an upstream.
453	async fn health(request: Request, next: Next) -> Response {
454	    if request.method() == Method::GET && request.uri().path() == "/health" {
455	        let headers =
456	            [(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/json"), (header::CACHE_CONTROL, "no-store")];
457	        return (StatusCode::OK, headers, json!({"status": "ok"}).to_string()).into_response();
458	    }
459	    next.run(request).await
460	}
461	
462	/// Require exactly one valid bearer on every HTTP route, including unknown paths.
463	async fn bearer(State(token): State<Arc<Secret>>, request: Request, next: Next) -> Response {
464	    let mut values = request.headers().get_all(header::AUTHORIZATION).iter();
465	    let authorized = match (values.next(), values.next()) {
466	        (Some(value), None) => {
467	            value.as_bytes().split_at_checked(7).is_some_and(|(scheme, candidate)| {
468	                scheme.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"bearer ")
469	                    && candidate.ct_eq(token.expose().as_bytes()).into()
470	            })
471	        }
472	        _ => false,
473	    };
474	    if authorized {
475	        return next.run(request).await;
476	    }
477	    let headers =
478	        [(header::WWW_AUTHENTICATE, "Bearer"), (header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/json")];
479	    let body = json!({"error": "authentication required"}).to_string();
480	    (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, headers, body).into_response()
481	}
482	
483	/// Build the authenticated Streamable HTTP application.
484	///
485	/// # Panics
486	/// At startup, when the TLS backend or the tool schema is broken.
487	pub fn router(settings: Settings) -> Router {
488	    let config = StreamableHttpServerConfig::default()
489	        .with_legacy_session_mode(false)
490	        .with_json_response(true)
491	        .with_sse_keep_alive(None)
492	        .with_allowed_hosts(settings.allowed_hosts.clone())
493	        .with_allowed_origins(settings.allowed_origins.clone())
494	        .enforce_origin_validation(); // an empty allow-list rejects, never disables
495	    let token = Arc::new(settings.bearer_token.clone());
496	    let broker =
497	        Broker { tools: Arc::new(tools(&settings)), client: Arc::new(MediaClient::new(settings)) };
498	    let service = StreamableHttpService::new(
499	        move || Ok(broker.clone()),
500	        Arc::new(LocalSessionManager::default()),
501	        config,
502	    );
503	    // The health layer runs outermost so its one exact route answers ahead of
504	    // the bearer boundary; every other method and path falls through to it.
505	    Router::new()
506	        .route_service("/mcp", service)
507	        .layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(token, bearer))
508	        .layer(middleware::from_fn(health))
509	}

gating. Argument types reject out-of-bounds input at parse time and
errors name the offending field.

newtype keeps credentials out of Debug output; item and Lidarr album
deletes share one two-phase flow with a five-minute HMAC-SHA256
confirmation bound to the exact action.
